economics_assumption: Future net revenue and contribution shares of payment revenue use observed channel-by-need-by-age shares, with the same group's observed renewal ages (age>=1) as fallback. Shares are fixed assumptions, not causally identified or assigned posterior uncertainty.
initialization: Seeded independent per-chain/site Uniform(-0.5,0.5) jitter in unconstrained parameter space
interpretation: Twelve-month contribution value, not an infinite-lifetime claim. Forecast cash payback is the first undiscounted crossing of the posterior-mean contribution path, not a distribution of realized payback times; payback_age is zero-based and payback_month counts receipts from 1. Discounting uses t=age+1. A separate flag identifies later recrossing below cost. Cohort random effects partially pool departures from the shared linear cohort trend. December 2025 has no observed renewal decisions; its retention forecast is inferred from other cohorts. No causal long-run campaign value is inferred from customer LTV.
model: Hierarchical shifted-Beta-Geometric retention + Gamma gross revenue; NumPyro NUTS

model_description.censoring: Pending renewals and future ages are unobserved, not failures. Age zero establishes acquisition and supplies no renewal trial. Churn is absorbing in this business.
model_description.forecast: Keep observed revenue and contribution; forecast recursively from the last observed survivors. All cohorts are valued over the same 12 monthly receipts, discounting at 1% per month. Forecast bands and the probability of nonnegative expected cash cover parameter uncertainty, not renewal/revenue process noise or all future business risk.
model_description.heterogeneity: Mean propensity varies with need, channel, cohort trend and a partially pooled cohort effect. Concentration varies with need and channel. Variance is mu*(1-mu)/(phi+1). Falling aggregate churn can reflect survivor selection, not improvement in each individual's loyalty.
model_description.retention: Each member has a persistent churn propensity. Within a cohort/need/channel cell, propensities follow one Beta distribution. After t-1 renewals, churn hazard is alpha/(alpha+beta+t-1); observed survivors follow a Binomial with the previous survivor count as its risk set.
model_description.revenue: Gross payment revenue follows a Gamma distribution with shape proportional to observed retained members. Expected revenue per retained member varies with log age, cohort trend, need and channel. Observed age-aligned net and contribution shares translate future gross revenue into economics.
model_description.source_adaptation: Retention extends Fader-Hardie sBG with mean/concentration parameterization, logit/log covariate links, a non-centered cohort effect on mean churn, grouped conditional Binomial renewal likelihood and NUTS estimation. Revenue adapts Orduz's Gamma structure but uses observed active counts in fitting, an additional per-member shape multiplier, a mean link without an age-by-cohort interaction, need/channel covariates and $100 scaling. Conditional on observed activity, the revenue and retention likelihoods have independent parameter blocks. The separate Orduz-inspired 4-hidden-unit Bayesian neural network is a retention comparison only; its cumulative-count likelihood is changed to conditional renewal trials.

uncertainty_label: Posterior parameter uncertainty conditional on the single-Beta model and fixed future economics; not a full predictive interval

valuation_backtest.baseline: Naive frozen last-three-period renewal rate and revenue per retained customer; a one-period cohort uses an explicit 0.8 renewal fallback.
